key_insight: OS-Symphony introduces an Orchestrator that coordinates granular visual-history curation and visual-aware tutorial retrieval, enabling vision-language computer-using agents to be robust in long-horizon workflows and to generalize to novel domains.
problem_solved: Addresses brittleness of current Computer-Using Agents caused by uncontrolled historical visual context and lack of visual-aware retrieval of task tutorials, which degrade performance on long workflows and unseen domains.
method: Orchestrator module that selects, prunes, and prioritizes historical visual context for downstream reasoning and action planning.
Visual-aware tutorial retrieval that matches current visual state to relevant external procedures and demonstrations to provide contextual guidance.
Tight integration enabling iterative planning and execution across long-horizon tasks, improving robustness and cross-domain generalization.
impact: Makes multimodal agents more reliable in real-world, multi-step tasks and easier to adapt to new environments, reducing failure modes and lowering the need for extensive domain-specific fine-tuning.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram showing the Orchestrator, visual-history curator, tutorial retriever, planner, and executor modules.
Timeline/sequence comparison: naive full-history vs. curated-history highlighting reduced noise and improved decision points.
Flowchart of visual-aware tutorial retrieval: input image -> visual embedding -> retrieval -> contextual instruction augmentation.
Performance chart (bars or heatmap) comparing robustness and generalization metrics across baselines and OS-Symphony.
paper_title: OS-Symphony: A Holistic Framework for Robust and Generalist Computer-Using Agent
paper_authors: Bowen Yang, Kaiming Jin, Zhenyu Wu, Zhaoyang Liu, Qiushi Sun
